clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read). The national emergency declared in Executive Order 13692 of March 8, 2015, for which this order takes additional steps, was continued for 1 year by the Presidential notice of February 18, 2026 (91 FR 8357, FR Doc. 2026-03502), which names Executive Order 13857 among the additional steps and so carries the emergency past the 2026-10-14 cutoff; the annual notices of 2019 through 2025 (FR Docs. 2019-04253, 2020-04822, 2021-04760, 2022-04908, 2023-04531, 2024-05036, 2025-03463) are also held, one for each year since the order. The Office of Foreign Assets Control notice of OFAC sanctions action (91 FR 54916, FR Doc. 2026-17263, published 2026-08-25) records a designation made on 2026-08-07 under section 1(a)(i) of Executive Order 13850 'as amended by Executive Order 13857', which shows the amended definition applied in 2026. The U.S. Code search covers release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09, and the eCFR/CFR search is a point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in the Code edition and none affecting this order is held. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends the clause.

inventory_overrides.reason: The preamble invokes IEEPA, the National Emergencies Act and 3 U.S.C. 301, recites the emergency of Executive Order 13692 and orders the steps that follow; it is the enacting command.
Section 1(a) is the only operative command: it amends the definition of the term Government of Venezuela in five named orders.
Section 2(a) is a rule of construction preserving agency authority and OMB functions.
Section 2(b) requires implementation consistent with law and subject to appropriations.
Section 2(c) disclaims any private right enforceable at law or in equity.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13857 of January 25, 2019 (84 FR 509), Taking Additional Steps To Address the National Emergency With Respect to Venezuela, is a short order. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13857.txt, 84 FR 509, PDF pages 1-2) carries the heading, the date January 25, 2019 and FR Doc. 2019-00615. The dossier's single inventory clause is a truncated slice of the preamble, so the inventory is corrected to five clauses: the preamble that invokes IEEPA and the National Emergencies Act and orders; section 1(a), the one operative command, which amends the definition of 'Government of Venezuela' in Executive Orders 13692, 13808, 13827, 13835 and 13850; section 2(a), the rule of construction; section 2(b), implementation consistent with law; and section 2(c), no private right. The order states no end. Its force depends on the amended orders and on the emergency declared in Executive Order 13692. The emergency was continued by the Presidential notice of February 18, 2026, and an OFAC action of 2026-08-07 applied Executive Order 13850 as amended by Executive Order 13857. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13857 finds the order's own page, the Federal Register copies, continuation notices, OFAC designation and general-license notices that describe other orders as amended by it, and 31 CFR part 591; none revokes, supersedes or amends it. The three bounded searches report no hit that ends it. The status on 2026-10-14 is operative for all five clauses. The held Federal Register text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected.
